title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: OTIS SINGS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Otis Greer, a garbage truck driver in Dubuque, Iowa. Six foot four, fifty-two years old.
Every morning at five, Otis sings in his truck, loud enough to rattle the trash cans.
But he has never once sung where a living person could hear him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE FLYER
segments.author: Ernest Hemingway
lines: One morning, a flyer was taped to a green bin. Community Chorus. Holiday concert. Low voices wanted.
Otis laughed. A trash man in a choir? Then he remembered a line his dad kept above the workbench, from Ernest Hemingway:
Courage is grace under pressure.
His hands were sweating. He called the number anyway, in his calmest voice.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: TOO LOUD
segments.quote: Harmony makes small things grow, lack of it makes great things decay.
segments.author: Sallust
lines: At the first practice, Otis opened his mouth and blew the music off three stands.
The director, Hazel, a tiny retired nurse, tapped her pencil and quoted Sallust, an old Roman historian:
Harmony makes small things grow, lack of it makes great things decay.
So Otis sang softer and listened to the man beside him. Forty voices became one. He got goosebumps.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE DOTS
segments.quote: Learning without thought is labor lost; thought without learning is perilous.
segments.author: Confucius
lines: Then came the sheet music. To Otis, the notes looked like ants on a fence.
He tried to fake it by guessing. Hazel said Confucius had a word for that:
Learning without thought is labor lost; thought without learning is perilous.
So he taped the notes to his dashboard and learned one line at every red light. Dubuque has plenty of red lights.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE CRACK
segments.quote: It is a mistake to suppose that men succeed through success; they much oftener succeed through failures.
segments.author: Samuel Smiles
lines: Two weeks before the concert, Hazel gave him a solo.
His voice cracked right in the middle. Somebody giggled. Otis wanted to quit.
His dad, Earl, eighty-one, who says about nine words a day, used four of them to point at a book by Samuel Smiles, an English writer:
It is a mistake to suppose that men succeed through success; they much oftener succeed through failures.
Otis sang that solo forty times that week. Mostly to recycling bins.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE ICE STORM
segments.quote: The occasion is piled high with difficulty, and we must rise with the occasion.
segments.author: Abraham Lincoln
lines: Concert night, an ice storm knocked the power out. The hall went dark.
Hazel almost canceled. Otis thought of the Abraham Lincoln poster at the city garage:
The occasion is piled high with difficulty, and we must rise with the occasion.
He called his crew. Three garbage trucks backed up to the windows, headlights on high.
Best stage lights in Iowa. A little smelly. Nobody complained.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE SOLO
segments.quote: Music can name the unnameable and communicate the unknowable.
segments.author: Leonard Bernstein
lines: In the front row sat his dad, arms folded. Otis had never once told him, I love you, Dad.
His knees shook. Hazel whispered a line from the great conductor Leonard Bernstein:
Music can name the unnameable and communicate the unknowable.
So Otis sang his solo straight to his dad. No crack.
Earl didn't say a word. He just hummed it all the way home.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Be brave. Blend in. Learn. Fail forward. Rise. Sing what you can't say.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Be brave under pressure. Blend in. Learn and think. Fail forward. Rise to the hard night. And sing what you can't say.
I sing in the shower too. My neighbors have started a petition.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
